title: OutcomeBound decision briefs v1
description: The input of `outcomebound brief`: the decision briefs an agent puts to a person, and the order among them. Every brief carries `id`, `heading` and `undo`; any other field may be left out, and a field left out writes nothing. A brief is drawn in the order a person decides: the question, `why_now`, `context`, `terms`, `diagram` and `picture`, `explore`, the `options` with the recommendation on the option it names, then the evidence. The command writes marks only from these fields, and also refuses what this schema cannot say: an option given as a list that is not exactly three strings, a pair in `facts`, `terms` or `order` that is not exactly two, a diagram edge that is not two or three, a string holding a line break, a control or format character or a mark's own glyph, a diagram label holding a double quote or an edge label holding a |, a `facts` label naming a line the renderer writes, a repeated id, an `order` label that is no brief's id, two `context` lists in a row, a `context` paragraph or item that starts with a markdown block opener, a way or a term with `*` or `_` at either edge, and a `picture` of only empty lines or with a line holding three backticks, a wide East Asian character, U+FE0F or U+20E3. It refuses with exit 1, naming the brief, a brief with two or more options and no `recommend` or no `recommend_way`, and a brief with none of `checked`, `not_checked` and `facts`. It does not vouch for what the text says: the verdicts under `checked` are the agent's own report of commands it ran, and the passed mark means only that every verdict given is PASS. A document written for an earlier release, with options as three-string lists and none of the newer fields, is still read.

briefs.description: The briefs, in the order they are put to the person.

id.description: The id the person answers by, such as D3: a letter followed by letters, digits and hyphens, unique in the document. The renderer joins it to the heading with the separator of the symbols it draws in, and `order` names briefs by it.

recommend.description: Why the recommendation is what it is; required where there are two or more `options`. Drawn under the option `recommend_way` names, behind the recommended mark; with no options or no named way, drawn as a paragraph of its own after the options.

recommend_way.description: The way of `options` that is recommended, spelled as it is there; required where there are two or more, and the recommendation is drawn under that option.

confidence.description: `fact` where a command the agent ran shows it, drawn as `a check shows this`, else `inferred`, drawn as `my judgment`; any other value, such as an older document's whole percentage followed by `(inferred)`, is drawn as given. Written only with `recommend`, at its end.

options.description: Every way forward, each either exactly three strings, [the way, what it leads to, its downside], or an object {way, leads_to, downside, choose_if} whose `choose_if` is optional: the condition, or what matters most to the person, under which a reasonable person picks it. The downside and the condition are written under their option behind marks of their own. The command refuses a single option, since a brief lays out options only where there are two or more.

way.description: The way forward in a few words; `*` or `_` at either edge is refused.

choose_if.description: When a reasonable person picks this way.

why_now.description: What waits on the answer, the state it waits in and what happens if no answer comes; drawn first after the question, as `Waiting on this`.

context.description: The context the person needs to judge, in short blocks. A block is a string, drawn as a paragraph, or a list of strings, drawn as a list. The command refuses an empty block or list, two lists in a row (a markdown view joins them into one; put a paragraph between), and a paragraph or item that starts with a markdown block opener.

terms.description: Each term the person may not know, as [term, meaning], drawn as a paragraph after the context. A term may not start or end with `*` or `_`.

picture.description: A small fixed-width figure for a before and after that edges show badly, drawn in a text fence after the diagram. The caption says what to look at. A line may be empty, and the lines may not all be empty; no line holds three backticks, a character of East Asian width W or F, U+FE0F or U+20E3 (an emoji drawn by default as text, which many fonts still draw two columns wide, is not detected).

explore.description: For a decision that is not simple, one line on what an interactive page would let the person try. The brief says the person can ask for it by the brief's id; with a question tool, the options gain a last choice, `Explore it first`.

checked.description: The verdict of every check the line names, and the line's text; the mark that means a check passed is written only where every verdict is PASS.

not_checked.description: What could not be checked, why, and what would settle it. A brief carries at least one of `checked`, `not_checked` and `facts`.

facts.description: Facts the agent knows that bear on the answer, as [label, text] pairs, each written as its own paragraph after Not checked; a label may not take the name of a line the renderer writes.

undo.description: Required on every brief: how it is undone, or, with `can_be_undone` false, what cannot be undone.

diagram.description: Drawn after the context and terms where order, dependency, flow or before/after is the point: a Mermaid flowchart where the surface renders Mermaid, and ASCII chains otherwise; every edge is drawn as given, and none is reduced away.

caption.description: The line written above the diagram, behind the picture mark; the mark is drawn only with a caption.

edges.description: Each edge as [from, to] or [from, to, label], in the order they are drawn; no label holds a double quote, and no edge label a |.

order.description: The order among the briefs, as [before, after] pairs: after waits on before.
